research_question: What is the effect of fenoldopam compared with control (placebo or saline) on development of acute kidney injury (AKI) across all patient populations?
positive_direction: A positive effect size (or risk ratio < 1.0) indicates a lower risk of acute kidney injury, favoring fenoldopam over control
search_queries: fenoldopam acute kidney injury randomized controlled trial
inclusion_criteria: Randomized or controlled clinical trials evaluating fenoldopam compared to placebo, saline, or standard care
Studies conducted in any clinical patient population at risk for acute kidney injury (e.g., cardiac surgery, non-cardiac surgery, sepsis, critical illness, contrast exposure)
Quantitative reporting of acute kidney injury (AKI) events and sample size per arm
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentary, narrative reviews, and animal or in vitro studies excluded)
No comparison between fenoldopam and an appropriate control condition (e.g., single-arm fenoldopam trials)
No extractable quantitative outcome data on the incidence or development of acute kidney injury (AKI)
Completely unrelated to fenoldopam administration or renal function outcomes
moderators_to_extract: patient population/clinical setting (cardiac surgery vs non-cardiac surgery vs ICU/critical illness vs contrast-induced nephropathy)
control type (placebo vs normal saline vs standard care)
AKI diagnostic criteria used (e.g., KDIGO, AKIN, RIFLE, or absolute serum creatinine elevation)
effect_size_note: Risk ratio (RR) pooled using event counts (patients developing AKI) and total sample sizes randomized per arm.
